title: Michael, Gabriel and Raphael (29 September)
hookLine: three angels with names: the protector, the messenger and the healer

cards: Angels in the Bible often appear, speak and vanish without giving a name.
When Jacob wrestles through the night with the one the prophet Osee later calls an angel, and asks its name, the answer is a question back: why do you ask?
So when an angel in scripture does say its name, people pay attention. The Catholic calendar keeps one feast for three of them together: one who fights, one who announces, one who heals.

teach.b: The word is archangel: a chief angel, one with a particular task. Start with Michael. In the book of Daniel he's a great prince who stands for his people.
In the Apocalypse, the book many call Revelation, Michael and his angels fight the dragon. Tradition reads his Hebrew name as a question: who is like God?
A small scene in the letter of Jude shows what that question means. Michael, the archangel, is arguing with the devil over the body of Moses. He could hurl an insult.
He says only, in the Douay-Rheims: "The Lord command thee." The warrior angel won't claim the fight as his own. Gabriel is the messenger.

He comes to Zechariah in the Temple and to Mary in Nazareth, and when he's doubted, he introduces himself: "I am Gabriel, who stand before God." His job is to carry news, often news that seems impossible.
Raphael is the healer and the traveling companion. His story is in the book of Tobias, a book Catholic and Orthodox Christians count as scripture and Protestant churches generally do not.
He walks beside young Tobias on a long journey, disguised as an ordinary man, and helps heal Tobias's blind father.
Only at the end does he reveal himself: "I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven, who stand before the Lord." A protector, a messenger, a healer.
And each one, in the end, points away from himself and toward God.

how: The feast of Saints Michael, Gabriel and Raphael, archangels, is kept on 29 September; some Catholics pray the Saint Michael prayer, attributed to Pope Leo XIII, at home, and some parishes say it after Mass.

o: the highest of all the choirs of angels
a chief angel, sent with a particular task
the spirit of a saint who died long ago

p: the protector who fights the dragon
the messenger to Zechariah and Mary
the healer who walks with Tobias

s: Gabriel is named in Luke's gospel
he introduces himself to Zechariah: I am Gabriel, who stand before God.
Raphael's story is in the book of Tobias
he travels with young Tobias, disguised as a man, and helps heal his father.
Michael insults the devil in Jude
he refuses to; he says only, the Lord command thee.

games.q: you're Michael the archangel, arguing with the devil over the body of Moses. what do you say?
o: hurl the worst accusation you can
games.why: Jude says Michael would not bring a railing accusation. He handed the matter to God: the Lord command thee.

practice: Some Catholics pray a short prayer to Saint Michael, asking him to defend us in the struggle with evil; if you pray, say it slowly now, or ask for protection in your own words, handing the fight to God the way Michael did.
If you don't pray, bring to mind one battle you're in right now, notice how much of it you've been trying to win alone, and let it rest for a moment.

wordCard.voice: Archangel. A chief angel with a task: Michael who protects, Gabriel who brings the message, Raphael who heals. Today's word.

orig.note: Michael's name in Hebrew, which tradition reads as a question: who is like God?

carryVoice: Your line: who is like god. A name that is a question. See you tomorrow.
